targets.review_note: Minimize retained wires instead of maximizing removed ones. A powered nonroot node costs one retained parent wire and forces its ancestors powered. Represent powered main-tree nodes on the source side of a cut and powered reserve-tree nodes on the sink side. Infinite main child->parent and reserve parent->child edges enforce ancestor closure. Unit main node->sink and source->reserve node edges charge exactly the retained wires. For each device, an infinite reserve-leaf->main-leaf edge prohibits both leaves being unpowered, while allowing either or both powered. Roots have no wire cost. Thus minimum cut is exactly minimum retained wires; subtract it from a+b-2. Dinic handles the sparse network without assuming parents precede children or relying on a particular planar drawing.
